statement: When mempalace mine ran as a subprocess, chromadb's global System cache (plus MemPalace's own backend client cache) kept serving the long-lived agent process a stale vector view, so a drawer filed mid-session was invisible to palace_search until the next restart.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Two caches conspire, so purge both
statement: _refresh_chroma_view() purges both the chromadb System cache and MemPalace's backend client cache on every successful mine, and add_drawer now verifies visibility by substance before claiming immediate recall.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] same-day content silently left the window
statement: Routine per-turn history trimming was count-based (max_messages=100), not token-aware: one tool-heavy cascade is 20-40 messages, so the working window covered roughly 3 real turns while most of a 1M-token context budget sat unused.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Default 150k, override via AGENT_HISTORY_TOKEN_BUDGET.
statement: Trimming now keeps the largest suffix within an estimated token budget (default 150k, clamped to 70% of the context window, floor 8192), with a 1000-message outer bound, verified by tests/test_measured_keep.py's 'THE WOUND ITSELF' regression test.
subject: self

statement: Before 1.12.1, a max_tokens recovery cascade (trim twice, then hard reset) dropped conversation messages from the front WITHOUT archiving them to the palace, unlike every other path that drops history — a runaway output cascade could eat an entire channel's verbatim history.
subject: self

statement: 1.12.1 archives the current message list to the palace at the first max_tokens retry (before any trim/reset), adds an output-ceiling early warning at two consecutive near-ceiling responses, and appends a post-recovery advisory naming the archive tag on subsequent turns.
subject: self

statement: An external code reviewer, Shravan Chaudhary (Co-Founder, Clodexa), identified that GaladrielAgent._trim_history's routine per-turn trim dropped the oldest slice in place with no archive, unlike every other history-dropping path, which already archived to the palace first.
subject: external

statement: The routine per-turn trim now archives the slice it is about to drop (fire-and-forget) and sets a post-recovery advisory, closing the asymmetry the external review identified; the 100-message trim cadence itself was deliberately left unchanged to avoid thrashing the prompt cache.
subject: self

statement: classify_command matched anchored tier patterns against the whole command string only, so a destructive command chained after a harmless one (e.g. a green head, `&& rm -rf` tail) was judged by its first, harmless segment.
subject: self

statement: Commands are now split on shell control operators, every segment is classified, and the maximum severity wins; several missing red-tier primitives (find -delete, xargs rm, mkfs, dd to devices) were added in the same change, regression-guarded by tests/test_safety_chaining.py.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] silently broke the entire red-tier approval gate before this existed
statement: approval_callback embedded the full raw shell command into a Discord approval message with no length guard; any red-tier command over roughly 2000 characters (a heredoc, a large diff) made channel.send() raise 400 Bad Request, so the approval prompt never rendered and the command could be neither approved nor denied.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] this only bounds what gets EMBEDDED in message
statement: _display_command() truncates only the text embedded in the Discord message (1500 chars, with a note of how much was cut); the de-duplication dict key and the command actually executed remain full-length, applied at all three embed sites.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] port from the living harness (2026-07-05): (1) heartbeat reconfigure-in-place
statement: A self-re-arming agent calling set_heartbeat(enabled=True) from inside its own running heartbeat tick used to cancel that very tick, killing the closing delivery message before it reached Discord.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] needs NO restart: update config, let the tick finish.
statement: set_heartbeat() now detects an in-flight tick and reconfigures in place (updates the stored interval/prompt and returns) instead of cancelling the running task; the loop re-reads its config every iteration, so the running tick still delivers its message before the new settings take effect.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] 2026-07-25, Lord Isildur
statement: On 2026-07-25 the operator (Lord Isildur), presented with two near-identical raw model ids as the /model picker's prominent label, meant to select Sonnet 4.6 and instead selected Opus 4.8.
subject: external

quote: [repo content] Friendly name LEADS (label); raw id is demoted to subtext.
statement: The /model picker now leads with the friendly display name as the Select option's label and demotes the raw model id to subtext, directly responding to the operator's misclick.
subject: self

subject: self

statement: tests/test_provider_parity.py mechanically guards the provider seam's byte-identical-wrapper contract by asserting the exact kwargs and cache_control markers passed to a mocked Anthropic client match the pre-seam call shape.
subject: self

statement: tests/test_journal.py exercises ConversationJournal's crash-tolerance (a torn tail line is skipped, not fatal) and its merge() union algebra across two independent item lists.
